correctness.rationale: The underlying draws, not the draws conditioned on their stopping count, are independent uniform marks. Independent rate-one Poisson streams give n exp(-tau_n) tending to Exp(1); conditional on the last first-arrival time and its index, there is one compulsory singleton and the other counts are independent positive-truncated Poisson variables. On compact positive windows of n exp(-tau_n), the conditional multinomial variances divided by (log n)^r tend uniformly to n exp(-tau_n)/r!, the scaled off-diagonal terms are O((log n)^((r+s)/2)/n), and the largest centered scaled summand is O((log n)^(-1/2)). The conditional characteristic-function expansion therefore has uniform vanishing remainder, yielding the joint Gaussian mixture when the window restriction is removed. The exact conditional mean minus the Poisson center is the singleton correction plus (n exp(-tau_n)-1)q_r(tau_n), negligible on every claimed scale. The independent rate-n clock has squared error H_n/n; the derivative of the center is O_p((log n)^r), so replacing tau_n by W_n/n incurs o_p((log n)^(r/2)) for fixed r. Exponential integration produces the stated characteristic function. For R>=2, distinct squares have positive covariance 1/(r!s!), although conditional coordinates are independent; for R=1 the dependence remark is vacuous. The frozen finite checker was inspected, not executed, and is not used as a proof of the limit.

The center differs from M_{n,r} by O_p(1) because n exp(-W_n/n) is tight, and log of the clock statistic recovers G_n.
